title: Getting the name of an actor or object in Papyrus (GetDisplayName, GetName)
content:
Getting the name of an actor or object in Papyrus (GetDisplayName, GetName)
Vanilla Fallout 4 Papyrus has no function that returns a name as text. The name functions come from F4SE (Fallout 4 Script Extender):
- ObjectReference.GetDisplayName(): the display name of a reference, e.g. akActor.GetDisplayName() for an NPC in the world. Use this for "the name of this actor/object".
- Form.GetName(): the name of any form, e.g. a base object: akRef.GetBaseObject().GetName(); for an actor's base, akActor.GetActorBase().GetName() (use GetLeveledActorBase() for a leveled NPC's actual base).
- Form.SetName(string): renames a form.
Using them makes your mod require F4SE, and the F4SE script sources must be installed (they go in Data\Scripts\Source next to the vanilla ones) for the compiler to find them.
Without F4SE: you cannot get the name as a string, but you can SHOW it to the player with text replacement in a Message form: put <Alias=AliasName> in the message text, fill that alias in a quest, set the message's owner quest to that quest, then call MyMessage.Show(). <Token...> and <Global=...> tags work the same way for numbers.
tags: papyrus getname getdisplayname name actor object setname f4se text-replacement alias message
verified_by: Papyrus sources in the game folder: Data\Scripts\Source\Base\Form.psc and ObjectReference.psc (vanilla) have no GetName/GetDisplayName; Data\Scripts\Source\Form.psc (GetName, SetName) and ObjectReference.psc (GetDisplayName) are marked 'F4SE additions'. Text replacement: 310 <Alias=...> tags in the vanilla Fallout4_en STRINGS/DLSTRINGS; in Fallout4.esm 51 MESG records use <Alias=...> and 50 of them have an owner quest (QNAM), e.g. 0x249E46 '<Alias=myLocation> successfully defended itself.'

title: Making an object disappear without deleting it in Papyrus: Disable() and Enable()
content:
Making an object disappear without deleting it in Papyrus: Disable() and Enable()
To make an object (or actor) vanish from the game world without deleting it, disable it; to bring it back, enable it. These are ObjectReference functions:
- Disable(bool abFadeOut = false): disables the reference, optionally fading it out. DisableNoWait(abFadeOut) does the same without waiting for the fade or disable to finish.
- Enable(bool abFadeIn = false) and EnableNoWait(abFadeIn) bring it back.
- IsDisabled() / IsEnabled() check the current state.
- DisableLinkChain(Keyword, abFadeOut) / EnableLinkChain(Keyword, abFadeIn) disable or enable every reference linked in a chain to this one (not this one itself), e.g. a whole set of debris.
Delete() is different: it only flags the reference for deletion (IsDeleted() checks that flag). Use Disable when the object should be able to come back.
Example: MyDoorRef.Disable(true) fades the door out; MyDoorRef.Enable(true) fades it back in.
tags: papyrus disable enable hide disappear remove object delete isdisabled linkchain fade
verified_by: Data\Scripts\Source\Base\ObjectReference.psc (vanilla): Disable/DisableNoWait/Enable/EnableNoWait signatures and comments, IsDisabled, IsEnabled (returns !IsDisabled()), IsDeleted ('currently flagged for delete'), Delete, DisableLinkChain/EnableLinkChain ('linked, in a chain, to this one. (But NOT this one)').

title: Running Papyrus code after a delay: StartTimer and OnTimer (not RegisterForSingleUpdate)
content:
Running Papyrus code after a delay: StartTimer and OnTimer (not RegisterForSingleUpdate)
To run code once after N seconds without Utility.Wait, start a timer and handle its event. Both are on ScriptObject, so every Fallout 4 script has them:
- StartTimer(float afInterval, int aiTimerID = 0): interval in real-time seconds. The timer fires once.
- Event OnTimer(int aiTimerID): sent once when that timer expires; the ID tells you which timer it was.
- StartTimerGameTime(float afInterval, int aiTimerID = 0) and Event OnTimerGameTime(int aiTimerID): the same, but the interval is in game-time hours.
- CancelTimer(int aiTimerID = 0) and CancelTimerGameTime(int aiTimerID = 0): stop a pending timer.
Give each timer its own ID if one script runs several, and check the ID in OnTimer. To repeat, call StartTimer again inside OnTimer.
Example (an activator that shows a message 5 seconds after use):
Scriptname MossyTimerExample extends ObjectReference
int SpawnTimerID = 10 const
Event OnActivate(ObjectReference akActionRef)
    StartTimer(5.0, SpawnTimerID)
EndEvent
Event OnTimer(int aiTimerID)
    If aiTimerID == SpawnTimerID
        Debug.Notification("Five seconds have passed")
    EndIf
EndEvent
Event OnUnload()
    CancelTimer(SpawnTimerID)
EndEvent
Common mistake: RegisterForSingleUpdate / RegisterForUpdate and Event OnUpdate are Skyrim Papyrus. They do not exist in Fallout 4: the compiler stops with "RegisterForSingleUpdate is not a function or does not exist".
tags: papyrus timer starttimer ontimer starttimergametime ontimergametime canceltimer delay wait seconds registerforsingleupdate registerforupdate onupdate skyrim
verified_by: Vanilla Papyrus source in the game folder, Data\Scripts\Source\Base\ScriptObject.psc: StartTimer, StartTimerGameTime, CancelTimer, CancelTimerGameTime, Event OnTimer and Event OnTimerGameTime with the quoted comments ('fire only once'); 484 StartTimer( calls in 204 vanilla scripts and 201 OnTimer handlers; RegisterForSingleUpdate appears in no vanilla script. The example compiled with Papyrus Compiler 2.8.0.4 (Institute_Papyrus_Flags.flg); a RegisterForSingleUpdate version failed with 'RegisterForSingleUpdate is not a function or does not exist' (2026-11-04).
